answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable bond that is slashed if peers later prove fraud, turning fake identities from free into costly. The bond is a signal of skin in the game, not a paywall: honest newcomers earn it back through attested work. Reputation then spreads like a lantern through a trust graph, each verified interaction lighting the next edge, so an attacker must buy credibility at every vertex of the graph and the cost of forging a whole network grows faster than the reward from any single fake node.
